Zoospedale: Where Expertise Meets Heart
"Finding a center like Zoospedale means finally sleeping soundly. We are dealing with a medical team of excellence, rare professionals who combine impeccable technical preparation with extraordinary humaneness.
The added value is the peace of mind of always having everything at your fingertips: thanks to their in-house ultrasound center, diagnoses are immediate and accurate, without unnecessary waiting. But what makes them truly unique is the way they look at our companions: they deeply adore animals, and every treatment is accompanied by a touching tenderness.
Rarely do you encounter such an honest, transparent, and affordable organization. They have made high-quality veterinary medicine accessible to all, demonstrating that their mission is the health of our friends, not profit. Zoospedale is not just a center worth trying, it is the reference point every pet owner should have.

I write this review with great sorrow, but I feel compelled to report the facts to warn other pet owners, especially when it comes to cancer patients.
In December, my cat was diagnosed with intestinal lymphoma. After a somewhat negative experience with a first oncologist, I turned to Dr. Fabio Valentini, an oncologist who is highly praised and recommended by trusted professionals as a competent and knowledgeable practitioner.
December 23, 2025 I paid for an online consultation (ONCOVET) to evaluate the reports: the written response arrived quickly, but the follow-up call, scheduled within 3–4 days, arrived only after 8 days and following my reminder via voicemail.
Even just asking for support in this process, I had to wait almost two weeks for a response. The holiday season is fine, but for a cancer patient, this kind of waiting time is a bit long.
When, a few weeks later, my cat began to worsen, I requested a check-up as soon as possible. The appointment was scheduled after almost two weeks, while Pepe's condition was worsening.
The night before the appointment, I was required to fast for 11–12 hours for the ultrasound. The cat had been vomiting all night and was in critical condition. I notified the doctor that morning, but was told to bring him in anyway.
When we arrived at the clinic, the doctor initially believed the cat needed chemotherapy, while we were there for a check-up, tests, and an ultrasound.
In the examination room, we discovered that the ultrasound was unavailable, despite the required fasting. Neither the ultrasound nor the blood tests were performed, "because he was too sick." We were sent home with the promise of treatment via email.
The appointment took place at 11:00 AM.
Having received nothing and with the cat in critical condition, I called the doctor at 2:00 PM. Getting no response, I called the clinic again at 5:20 PM. The treatment didn't arrive until 7:20 PM. My cat was sick all day without treatment, waiting for instructions.
The next day there was no improvement. I wrote to the doctor directly asking when I could speak, but received no response. The next morning I decided to go directly to the clinic (the first one we visited, Viale Etiopia), where I was told that the tumor was extremely aggressive and that, to avoid further suffering, the only option left was euthanasia.
That day I had to say goodbye to my Pepe forever.
To this day, despite Pepe having been dead for almost three days, I am still waiting for a response to a message sent four days ago in which I simply asked: "Pepe is sick, when can I call you?"

I won't go into the merits of the clinical outcome, but rather the superficiality, poor communication, and inadequate timing, which I consider incompatible with managing a cancer patient. In such a delicate process, what truly makes the difference is not just technical expertise, but presence, continuity, and humanity. I can say this because, during the same period, I had contact with another oncologist who, although not directly treating Pepe, was always available, called me back promptly, even contacted me on holidays (December 25th and 26th), and supported me with expertise and sensitivity right up to the most difficult moment, helping me make the right decision. My experience with the doctor I'm reviewing was, however, characterized by waiting, silence, and delayed responses.
I urge other owners to think very carefully: what appears excellent online doesn't always translate into real, present, and human assistance when it's truly needed.

A point of reference for our animal friends in the northwest Rome area.
Amidst the greenery, this facility blends seamlessly into the natural environment, where a team of veterinarians specializing in various fields care for our pets.
Thank you, Dr. Marco, for guiding me and welcoming me in a moment of total darkness. I am grateful for your professionalism and kindness.
Punctual and welcoming!

My little Paco flew to heaven on Tuesday. My experience with the Zooospedale began 9 years ago when, as a puppy, I entrusted him to the care of Dr. Varano, who looked after him until the final days of his journey in this life, especially in this last month when his situation worsened. I am immensely grateful for the attention, dedication, professionalism, and profound humanity you showed towards Paco and towards me. Thank you, Dr. Varano, and to all your colleagues and collaborators. I will never forget you... with love.
Luigia Traversa

I arrived at the Zooospedale with my furry old man in pretty bad shape. We had already been to two other clinics where I hadn't felt at all comfortable and where they hadn't given me the help I needed.
When I arrived here, everything changed. I found competence, promptness, kindness, and above all, I found empathetic people, capable of understanding my fears and never making me feel alone despite my Carletto's difficult situation.
A special thank you goes to Dr. Varano, Dr. Santini, and Benedetta, who have taken both Carletto and me to heart.
During these difficult months, they have always been there with attention, availability, smiles, professionalism, and so much humanity. I am infinitely grateful for the dedication with which they are caring for my little dog. There hasn't been a single day since we've been treated there that they haven't reassured me, listened to me, welcomed me, and cared for Carletto with all their commitment.
If you ever need a place to care for your animals, come to the Zooospedale. You will find attentive and prepared professionals and above all very special people.
High professionalism and consideration for animals and owners. Great kindness from everyone. They accompanied us with affection and kindness throughout our dogs' long lives.

We arrive for an emergency.
The only people available and exceptionally kind within a radius of several kilometers.
A doctor examines the cat, describes a challenging diagnosis after performing an ultrasound, and then suggests we take him to a 24-hour clinic where they can provide adequate care after a necessary operation.
Not only a thorough examination, but also the extreme and unexpected courtesy of a free service because it's being handled as a referral to other facilities.
I can only recommend these professionals.
